newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Downsizing BTR raises US$300 mln in Taiwan selloff.
newsitem.headline: Downsizing BTR raises US$300 mln in Taiwan selloff.

text.p: British-based industrial conglomerate BTR Plc has sold off its majority stakes in three Taiwan petrochemical firms, raising some US$300 million in a corporate realignment, executives said on Monday.
Union Petrochemical and USI Far East, in a notice to Taiwan's stock exchange, identified themselves as the buyers of BTR's stakes in Taita Chemical, Asia Polymer and China General Plastics.
The two buyers paid T$2.707 billion, or about US$98 million, and said the remainder of the US$300 purchase price would be raised through bank loans, USI Far East spokeswoman Chu Shu-yun told Reuters.
"The T$2.7 billion is self-owned capital," Chu said. "We will seek bank loans to complete the total US$300 million purchase price."
The transactions would be completed by the end of 1996, the purchasing companies said.
BTR had held controlling 51 percent stakes in Taita and Asia Polymer and a 31 percent stake in China General Plastics, the notification said.
Taiwan media said BTR's effective stake in General Plastics was also 51 percent, with the balance held through affiliates.
